# Create a soothing bedtime story routine with Alexa

Imagine tucking your child into bed and simply saying, "Alexa, bedtime story." In a few minutes you can set up a routine in the Alexa app that lowers the volume and starts a story with that one phrase. Once it's saved, you can use it every evening, creating a small, calm ritual for your family.

## Before you start
- The **Alexa app** on your phone or tablet, signed in to the same Amazon account as your Echo.
- An **Echo** (or other Alexa device) in your child's room or nearby.
- About **10 minutes**.

## Step 1 — Open Routines in the Alexa app
Open the **Alexa** app. At the bottom of the screen, tap **More**, then tap **Routines**. This is where all your routines live. If you can't find More at the bottom, check whether your app needs an update in your phone's app store.

You'll know it worked when you see the Routines page, with or without routines already on it.

## Step 2 — Start a new routine
Tap the **+** in the top-right corner of the Routines page. A new, empty routine opens. If the app asks you for a name at any point, type something you'll recognize later, such as **Bedtime Story**.

💬 Example: name it `Bedtime Story`.

You'll know it worked when you see an empty routine with a place to add an event and a place to add an action.

## Step 3 — Choose the phrase that starts it
Tap **Add an event** and follow the steps in the app to choose what starts your routine. To start it with your voice, choose the option for a spoken phrase and type the words you'll say **after** the wake word — for example **bedtime story**. Don't type "Alexa" itself: the wake word is how you get Alexa's attention, the phrase is what comes after it.

💬 Example: type `bedtime story` as the phrase.

You'll know it worked when your phrase appears as the event at the top of the routine.

## Step 4 — Add a calm volume first
Tap **Add an action** and follow the steps in the app. Alexa routines can control your devices' settings as well as play content. Look for the action that sets your Echo's **volume**, pick a low level, and choose the Echo in your child's room if the app asks which device to use. Doing this first means the story never starts at full blast.

You'll know it worked when the volume setting appears as the first action in your routine.

## Step 5 — Add the story as the last action
Tap **Add an action** again and look for the **custom action**, which lets you type anything you could normally say to Alexa. Type **tell me a bedtime story**. If your family already uses a particular story skill, you can type the phrase you'd normally use to open it instead. One rule from Amazon's help: a custom action has to be the **last** action in a routine, so add it after the volume step.

💬 Example: type `tell me a bedtime story` as the custom action.

You'll know it worked when your routine lists two actions: the volume first, then your typed request.

## Step 6 — Save and test it
Tap **Save**. Now go to the Echo and say **"Alexa, bedtime story."** Alexa should lower the volume and start the story. If nothing happens, open the routine again, check the phrase for typos, and make sure the routine is set to run on the device you're talking to.

💬 Example: say `Alexa, bedtime story` to the Echo.

You'll know it worked when Alexa runs both actions after your phrase.

## Step 7 — Let it end on its own (optional)
If your child likes to fall asleep to something playing, Amazon's help lists a **sleep timer** command that stops playback after a set time. After the story, say for example **"Alexa, set a sleep timer for 30 minutes"**, and whatever is playing stops by itself.

💬 Example: say `Alexa, set a sleep timer for 30 minutes`.

## Common mistakes
- **Typing "Alexa" into the phrase:** the phrase is only what comes after the wake word. Type `bedtime story`, then say "Alexa, bedtime story".
- **Putting the custom action first:** Amazon's help says a custom action has to be the last action in a routine. Keep the volume step first and the story last.
- **Testing on the wrong Echo:** if you have several devices, check which one the routine is set to use — otherwise the story may start in another room.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can now start a calming storytime for your child with a single voice command, freeing up your hands and giving you a few extra minutes to get ready for bed yourself.
- **For your business or work:** While this specific routine is personal, the same idea — one phrase, several actions — can be used for a "start my workday" routine that plays the news and reads your calendar.
- **If you're just getting started:** This is an easy first routine: one phrase, two actions, and you've turned your Echo into a helpful part of the evening without any technical skills.

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app, tap **More → Routines → +**, and name the routine "Bedtime Story." Under **Add an event**, set the spoken phrase to `bedtime story`. Add a low volume action, then a custom action with `tell me a bedtime story` as the last step, and tap **Save**. Say "Alexa, bedtime story" to your Echo to test it.
